maya: quick thread — i ran an end-to-end profile comparing INT8 vs FP8 for KV cache (both frozen-kv and streaming decode). saw interesting latency/memory/quality tradeoffs, tagging @joel @sylvie @alex for kernel/batching context

joel: TL;DR numbers from my run (baseline = FP32 KV):
- FP32 KV: mem per request ~ 1.00x, tail decode latency ~ 0ms delta (baseline)
- INT8 KV (symmetric per-tensor quant): mem ~ 0.72x, avg per-token decode latency +5ms at seq<=128, +14ms at seq>=512
- FP8 KV (E4M3-like dynamic range): mem ~ 0.79x, avg per-token decode latency +2ms at seq<=128, +6ms at seq>=512
- Throughput (tokens/s) for batched decode (batch size 8, seq 64): FP32 12.5k, FP8 12.1k, INT8 11.3k
- Observed quality: INT8 shows occasional 1-2 token repetition increases in long-context (>1k) runs. FP8 shows ~0.4% BLEU/ROUGE drop on our eval prompts vs FP32.

sylvie: can you paste the kernel selector logs? curious which GEMM paths are used for INT8 vs FP8 on A100/RTX6000.

joel: pasted snippets below (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-12T15:04:21Z] kernel_select: matmul.shape=(4096,4096) dtype=fp8 device=sm80 -> selected=matmul_fused_fp8_sm80 (fastpath fused-contract)
[2026-02-12T15:04:21Z] kernel_select: kv_matmul.shape=(4096,512) dtype=int8 device=sm80 -> selected=matmul_int8_accfp32_v2 (uses int8 gemm + fp32 acc)
[2026-02-12T15:04:21Z] runtime: kv_cache.mode=quantized, dequantize_on_read=false, fused_attention=true
```

alex: couple notes on where the latency comes from:
- INT8 path uses unpack/pack + scaled accumulators on the decode hot path for KV reads when we do partial dequantization. that costs ~3-8us per KV read on our microbench (amplifies at long seq).
- FP8 path benefits from fused fp8 matmul kernels — fewer kernel launches and less memory traffic — but calibration noise causes extra attention-softmax variance, which explains the small quality loss.

joel: i also tried two calibration modes: per-tensor symmetric (fast) vs per-channel (slower, more accurate). results: per-channel int8 reduced decode quality regressions but increased CPU calibrate time and slightly higher memory (scales table). FP8 benefits less from per-channel; dynamic scaling handled most outliers.

sylvie: what about batching heuristics? static window vs continuous batching?

joel: tested three heuristics with INT8 KV:
- static_time_window(5ms): good for low concurrency, loses because short windows break batching for long-decode streams -> throughput drop ~10%
- continuous_batching(adaptive): we use token-aware flush — maintained throughput and reduced added latency (~+1-3ms for FP8 path, +3-8ms for INT8)
- prefix_caching optimized: when prefix in KV hit rate >80% we skip full dequantize path and use cached fp32 prefixes -> recovers ~6-10% latency for INT8 on repeated convo workloads

perf-bot: profiling summary (automated):
- end-to-end p95 decode latency (seq=512, bs=4): FP32 420ms, FP8 462ms (+10%), INT8 490ms (+17%)
- memory footprint (model+kv): FP32 12.8GB, FP8 10.1GB (-21%), INT8 9.1GB (-29%)
- tokens/s (steady state, bs=8, seq=64): FP32 12.5k, FP8 12.1k, INT8 11.3k

maya: interesting — INT8 gives best memory but worst decode p95. FP8 is balanced. any obvious regression causes?

sylvie: i suspect two components: (1) per-request dequant cost (INT8) and (2) kernel fallback patterns when sequence lengths step over thresholds (we saw fallback to slower kernel for matmul sizes >4096). joel, can you repro kernel fallback with debug selector enabled?

joel: enabled debug selector and reproduced this snippet:
```
[selector] matmul dims 8192x4096 -> attempted matmul_int8_accfp32_v2, nvcc kernel failed heuristics -> fallback to matmul_int8_generic (slower)
```
That fallback explains step latency regression at larger seqs.

alex: action items i propose:
1) quick: enable prefix_caching early-path for INT8 to avoid per-dequant on 80% repeated prefixes. (low risk)
2) medium: audit kernel selector heuristics so we avoid unnecessary fallbacks for common matmul shapes (possibly increase workspace or change alignment)
3) longer: implement hybrid KV layout: store recent prefixes as fp16/packed-fp8 hot cache and cold KV as INT8 to reduce hot-path dequant.

maya: sounds good. joel — can you attach the raw perf artifacts to the thread and mark hot traces where the per-KV read time accumulates? sylvie — can you look at selector heuristics and list safe parameter bumps? alex — i'll sketch hybrid layout prototype next week.

joel: uploading perf tarball to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/1760876543-kv-quant-e2e.tar.gz (contains nvprof traces, kernel selector logs, and decode-level flamegraphs).

sylvie: FYI — i already have a small patch that raises int8_workspace_bytes_threshold for sm80 by 256k which prevents that specific fallback in my local runs. will PR and add perf numbers.

maya: thanks all. if anyone hits an urgent regression in nightly perf, ping here and i'll triage. :thumbsup:
